content.title: About
content.content: Butter replacement powder (4921) is a dry product made from vegetable oils, emulsifiers and stabilizers. When reconstituted with water it forms a creamy spread that mimics the taste and texture of regular butter. It is used in cooking, confectionery and food manufacturing as an alternative to traditional butter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powder is easy to transport and store because it does not require refrigeration.
It is a popular ingredient in vegan recipes, being completely plant‑based.
Properly reconstituted, it retains a buttery flavor without the typical oil aftertaste.
The powder allows precise dosing, simplifying calorie control in dishes.
Unlike solid butter, the powder has a much longer shelf life.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Most of the fats are poly‑ and monounsaturated, making it more heart‑friendly than regular butter.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Being plant‑derived, it contains no cholesterol.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Formulations often include added B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The powdered form hydrates quickly and is gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Supports dietary restrictions
items.content: Suitable for vegans, lactose‑intolerant individuals and anyone avoiding dairy.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: The product may contain soy, sunflower or other allergens; check the label if you have sensitivities.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some versions include flavor enhancers and preservatives that may not be suitable for sensitive stomachs.

items.title: May not fully replace butter in baking
items.content: Differences in fat crystal structure can require recipe adjustments for optimal texture.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix 1 tsp of powder with 8–10 ml of water, whisk until a smooth creamy consistency is achieved. The resulting spread can be used on bread, in sauces, creams, baked goods and for sautéing. Increase the powder‑to‑water ratio for a firmer texture if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Shelf life is typically 12–18 months. After opening, use within 3 months and protect from moisture.
